title: Most babies sit without support by about 9 months
summary: Most babies sit without support by about 9 months, the US CDC says.
body: Sitting without support is a movement line on the CDC 9-month page, grouped with what most babies do by that age. The page also lists getting to a sitting position by herself as a separate line. This card is only the unsupported sit, not the getting-there line. An American checklist printed this age. It is not a posture score, and another country may print a different month.

sources.title: Milestones by 9 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: Movement line: Sits without support. Getting to sitting is a different line and is not the claim.
